name: The Censor
rule: One random number scores no points this Puzzle
entrance: A black 0 pts band settles onto playable Hand copies of the saved censored digit with the shared 0.23-second object arrival.
trigger: The Hand band shows the zero price before play. When the censored digit actually scores, its receipt strikes the original Points and stamps the actual zero over 0.22 seconds.
persistent: The header names the censored digit; its Hand price band stays readable beneath the number. No marks are painted over board numbers.
notes: The band is a public rule cue, not a prediction of correctness. It is omitted outside scoring play and when an independent Hand bar takes precedence.

name: The Editor
rule: Hand size -1
entrance: A small folded-slot paper object settles into the Hand margin over 0.23 seconds.
trigger: No additional boss-specific triggered motion.
persistent: A folded corner and current Hand capacity identify the missing slot.

name: The Deadline
rule: 8 Turns instead of 10
entrance: The Turn label and cut margins settle in with a short tilt and drop.
trigger: The standard Turn number updates after banking.
persistent: Cut red margins remain beside the 8-Turn label.

name: The Fog
rule: Marked squares are hidden this Puzzle
entrance: Two soft mist layers roll in from opposite sides over 0.65 seconds.
trigger: Slow gray and faster ivory wisps drift continuously below the printed digits.
persistent: Fog conceals Markers while numerals and selections stay crisp.
notes: Ambient motion pauses while covered, in the background, in Low Power Mode, or with in-game Reduced Motion/background motion disabled.

name: The Critic
rule: Wrong-placement penalty doubled
entrance: No separate boss entrance; the ordinary page reveal is used.
trigger: A wrong tile follows the existing return-to-Pool/Hand flight with the actual doubled debit printed beneath it.
persistent: Header states that wrong-placement penalties double.
notes: No unique Critic entrance or bespoke penalty animation was added; the shared wrong-number motion carries the larger penalty.

name: The Mirror
rule: No Line Clear bonuses this Puzzle
entrance: A small doubled paper receipt in the header carries a LINE 0 stamp.
trigger: A committed suppressed Line Clear pulses the header stamp through anticipation, contact, and settle. Its scoring receipt strikes the original bonus and prints the actual zero over 0.22 seconds.
persistent: The zero receipt stays off the board. The header says Line bonus: 0 and that placements still score.
notes: Full Clear bonuses are unaffected. The cue never paints over Sudoku numbers or previews placement correctness.

name: The Paywall
rule: All Clues disabled, including Buff-granted
entrance: If owned Clue charges expose the Clue control, a small lock seal settles onto it.
trigger: The seal remains still when a blocked Clue is inspected.
persistent: The Clue control stays sealed; Buff details explain the restriction.
notes: With no Clue charges, the conditional Clue control is absent, so its entrance seal is not visible.

name: The Erratum
rule: No Tosses this Puzzle
entrance: A crossed TOSS paper tab drops and straightens onto the existing Toss control.
trigger: No additional boss-specific triggered motion.
persistent: Toss stays disabled with the crossed tab visible.

name: The Collector
rule: This Puzzle's payout includes no interest
entrance: No separate boss entrance; the ordinary page reveal is used.
trigger: On a real payout, the saved interest amount is crossed out to zero over 0.20 seconds.
persistent: The payout retains the crossed interest alongside unchanged base and other earnings.
notes: If the payout had no suppressed interest, there is no interest-crossing animation.

name: The Final Draft
rule: The target is four times what it would be
entrance: At a fresh encounter, the original target transforms to its authoritative fourfold target over 0.35 seconds; a temporary ×4 paper tab appears.
trigger: No additional boss-specific triggered motion.
persistent: The final fourfold target remains in the normal score row.
notes: Save/resume displays the final target directly and does not replay the expansion.

name: The Executive Editor
rule: One triggered Bookmark sleeps each Turn; passive upgrades stay active
entrance: The header identifies the actual sleeping slot with a folded paper copy and REST band.
trigger: At the engine-selected sleep change, the exact owned Bookmark dims and folds over 0.20 seconds. Its REST band moves with the affected copy, not with an assumed inventory index.
persistent: The sleeping copy stays visibly marked; the header states its current slot. Passive upgrades remain active.
notes: The sleep cue communicates disabled triggered effects only. It does not imply that the player lost the Bookmark or its passive upgrades.

name: The Fine Print
rule: No Buff can be spent this Puzzle
entrance: Lock seals settle onto the owned Buffs and empty Buff slots over 0.23 seconds.
trigger: No additional boss-specific triggered motion.
persistent: Buff slots remain sealed and owned Buffs subdued.

name: The Budget Cut
rule: All score multipliers are cut in half
entrance: No separate boss entrance; the ordinary page reveal is used.
trigger: At an actual bank, the final Mult receipt moves slightly and a torn edge draws beneath its halved value over 0.22 seconds.
persistent: The receipt shows the exact Mult before and after the cut.
notes: A live preview does not replay the bank-only cut effect.

name: The Shredder
rule: Up to three squares are fouled each Turn for two Turns; one blank stays free
entrance: A falling ink droplet spreads into a wet, irregular pool on each newly fouled square.
trigger: Each Turn, newly committed fouls get one 0.62-second droplet/spread; older pools remain until their saved expiry.
persistent: Only truly fouled squares contain settled ink with a small wet highlight.
notes: Saved pools appear settled on resume; a remount never invents a fresh impact.

name: Natural Born Accountant
rule: Every placement costs a coin, even if you have none
entrance: The header presents a brass coin slot and the per-placement charge; the ordinary page reveal is used.
trigger: Each committed coin-cost operation makes the header coin rise, turn, drop into the slot, and reset over 0.52 seconds. The existing balance receipt also shows the actual debit, including a wrong placement.
persistent: The slot reads −1 coin / fill and counts actual charges this Turn. The balance can show debt; Keep Filling still shows the active placement charge.
notes: Motion is keyed to the saved scoring operation ID, never to preview score changes. No coin flies over the board.

name: Tik Tak
rule: Four minutes for the whole Puzzle
entrance: The ordinary header shows the live 04:00 clock; no separate entrance.
trigger: The clock turns amber at 60 seconds, red at 30, and gives one brief scale pulse at 30 and 10 seconds.
persistent: A large monospaced countdown replaces the boss rule line.
notes: The clock reads active gameplay time; Settings pauses it. No decorative second timer is used.

name: Handy Dandy
rule: Up to two cards are barred each Turn; your whole Hand is never barred
entrance: Paper lock tabs settle onto the exact barred Hand copies.
trigger: When bars change each Turn, the old tabs leave and new tabs enter over 0.20 seconds; committed Hand feedback uses the shared barred-card pop.
persistent: The exact barred copies remain sealed, with their number glyphs readable.

name: Gray the Garry
rule: A row is barred each Turn, unless it holds every remaining blank
entrance: Terracotta bricks drop onto the actually barred blank squares one by one, 0.11 seconds apart.
trigger: Old bricks lift and fade before the next row receives new drops. Each impact has a small rebound and dust that fades over 0.34 seconds.
persistent: Settled clay bricks and contact shadows cover only barred blanks.
notes: Given or filled squares never receive bricks. Save/resume starts settled.

name: Garry the Gray
rule: A box is barred each Turn, unless it holds every remaining blank
entrance: Terracotta bricks drop onto the actually barred blank squares one by one, 0.11 seconds apart.
trigger: Old bricks lift and fade before the next box receives new drops. Each impact has a small rebound and dust that fades over 0.34 seconds.
persistent: Settled clay bricks and contact shadows cover only barred blanks.
notes: Given or filled squares never receive bricks. Save/resume starts settled.

name: The Galley Queue
rule: Your two oldest available cards play first. Use one to open the next card.
entrance: Sage PLAY trays and wider locked WAIT sleeves settle onto the exact Hand copies with the shared 0.23-second object arrival.
trigger: When eligibility changes, old bands slide down and the next eligible copies receive PLAY bands with a 0.38-second spring. Numbers shift slightly upward to keep the labels clear.
persistent: PLAY and WAIT are printed on the cards themselves; a separate outer selection ring identifies the selected card. Queue order follows arrival identity even when the Hand is sorted.
notes: Independent bars keep their ordinary crossed-card treatment. Release Note can make an otherwise waiting exact copy playable; visual state follows that engine permission.

name: The Bookends
rule: Only the lowest and highest available numbers can play.
entrance: Brass side posts and LOW/HIGH bands settle onto eligible extrema; middle cards get locked WAIT sleeves.
trigger: Posts and bands update with a 0.38-second spring when the available lowest or highest digits change. The existing card identity and display order stay intact.
persistent: All eligible duplicate extrema show LOW or HIGH. If all available digits match, they show PLAY; a Release Note bypass on a middle card also shows PLAY.
notes: The card selection ring remains separate from the brass bookends. No visual rearrangement changes eligibility.

name: The Reprint Ban
rule: A number you filled this Turn waits while a new number can play. When only repeats remain, they open.
entrance: Available cards enter with sage PLAY bands; restored or already used restricted copies show red locked USED bands.
trigger: After a correct fill, repeated copies that now must wait receive red USED bands through a 0.38-second spring transition. Bands reopen to PLAY when repeats become available, and close again if a new available digit is drawn.
persistent: The header names currently waiting digits and asks for a new number, or says Repeats are open when a repeat is actually playable.
notes: Correct Clue fills count as used; wrong attempts do not. Independent bars and exact-copy Release Note bypasses are respected. End Turn clears the used-digit restriction.

name: The Rebinder
rule: At End Turn, return leftovers to the Pool before drawing a fresh Hand
entrance: No separate boss entrance; the ordinary page reveal is used.
trigger: At End Turn, the exact leftover tiles shrink, rotate and fade toward the Hand’s Pool edge, followed by the existing fresh-card arrivals.
persistent: The header explains that leftovers return before refill.
notes: This uses the shared number-return motion with actual outgoing card identities; there is no visible Pool label.

name: The Late Courier
rule: Automatic bonus draws arrive after banking and count toward refill
entrance: No separate boss entrance; the ordinary page reveal is used.
trigger: Folded draw tickets rise in as draws are owed, then fly upward/fade on delivery while actual cards enter the Hand.
persistent: A small ticket count sits on End Turn until the draws are delivered.
notes: Tickets show counts, never the future hidden digits.

name: The Collator
rule: Half your Hand waits for 2 correct fills or an empty first packet
entrance: Open packet cards enter with sage PLAY bands. Waiting packet cards wear broader paper sleeves with a lock and two progress circles.
trigger: Correct fills update the two circles. When the engine opens the packet, the waiting sleeve slides away and PLAY arrives with the shared 0.38-second spring.
persistent: The digits remain face-up above the bands; the header reports packet progress or that both packets are open.
notes: Packet release also occurs when no independently available first-packet card remains. This is a changing sleeve, not a separately animated wrapper tear.

name: The Page Cutter
rule: Every 4 correct fills end the Turn; start with 4 extra Turns
entrance: Four numbered paper tickets and scissors appear in the header with the visible caption 4 fills → bank.
trigger: Tickets fill as the committed correct-fill count advances, using the shared 0.3-second status transition. The real automatic Turn boundary resets the tickets; the existing short cutter sweep remains beside the Turn label.
persistent: The four-ticket progress display explains the automatic bank before the fourth fill is made.
notes: This pass adds visible progress, not a separate lever-pull or full-screen cut scene. Banking remains an engine action, including correct Clue fills.

name: The Chain Stitcher
rule: Follow your last placement: same row, column or box earns full placement Points; elsewhere earns half. Clues don't move the link.
entrance: Before the first unaided fill, the header asks the player to place a number to start. A resumed anchor displays its settled gold scoring region directly.
trigger: Each later correct non-Clue fill moves the brass anchor and gold full-price region. A transient 0.8-second stitch links the old and new anchors; a disconnected fill uses a broken red stitch and a brief half-points tag. The existing actual halving receipt remains.
persistent: Gold wells identify available blanks sharing the anchor row, column or box, distinct from sage matching-number selection. The header key reads Lit ×1 / Other ½ with Placement points. No persistent connecting line remains.
notes: Geometry never predicts a correct digit. Clues and wrong/rejected attempts do not move the anchor. Passage-enabled squares are included. The region and key stop during frozen scoring; first fill each Turn is full, and simultaneous clear bonuses are unchanged.

name: The Return Slip
rule: Wrong cards return sealed until next Turn; normal penalties still apply
entrance: No separate boss entrance. Any saved sealed Hand copies appear with full-width red SEALED bands rather than tiny lock tabs.
trigger: A wrong card uses the existing exact-copy return flight and normal penalty. Its SEALED band enters with the shared 0.38-second spring and leaves when the next Turn releases it.
persistent: Returned numbers remain readable above their red SEALED bands. The header reports how many cards are sealed.
notes: The seal does not cancel wrong-placement penalties. Exact-copy Release Note permission clears the visible blocked treatment while it applies.

name: The Orphan Line
rule: Banking costs 20 queued Points per leftover card, up to 100
entrance: A paper-stack symbol and live red Points debit appear in the existing header beside the leftover-card count.
trigger: The prospective debit updates before End Turn as Hand size and queued Points change. Committed scoring and Points changes receive 0.3-second numeric transitions; banking retains the actual torn-receipt debit.
persistent: The player can see the exact capped debit for ending now. Accessibility states that it is applied to Points before Mult.
notes: There are no separate debt tickets on every Hand card. The displayed debit includes the current queued Points cap and is not a subtraction from final multiplied score.

name: The Serial Publisher
rule: Bank up to a third of target. Carry overflow; Full Clear pays all
entrance: The existing header shows separate bordered BANK and stacked HOLD paper slips as soon as the scoring preview is available; no separate entrance cinematic.
trigger: Live paid and carried amounts update from the real settlement preview with 0.3-second numeric transitions. Banking retains the actual banded settlement receipt.
persistent: BANK and HOLD display the exact score paid now versus carried after banking. During Keep Filling, saved carry remains visible as HELD with Full Clear pays.
notes: The held stack is a layered paper drawing, not a separate travelling-score animation. All values come from the saved state and pure ledger preview; Full Clear pays remaining carry.

name: The Bindery
rule: Bookmarks pin on your first action; odd Turns read forwards, even Turns backwards
entrance: Before the first action, the header shows that Bookmarks can be arranged. Pinning settles the stitched thread beneath the inventory.
trigger: Actual Bookmark receipts move a brass-and-wood shuttle to the paid source in engine scoring order. Each passage has a short lift, contact, and settle; the header changes its read direction with the Turn.
persistent: The stitched inventory and pin indicate that order is fixed for the Puzzle. Odd Turns read rightwards; even Turns read leftwards.
notes: Shuttle motion follows committed source receipts. It does not reorder Bookmarks or run an idle loop.

name: The Embargo
rule: Use preparation Buffs before your first placement attempt each Turn
entrance: No separate boss entrance; the ordinary page reveal is used.
trigger: After the first placement attempt, eligible preparation Buffs dim and small lock seals slide/fade in; next Turn clears them.
persistent: Only preparation Buffs affected by the engine restriction are sealed.
notes: Embargo uses the existing Buff-slot seal transition rather than a separate embargo banner.

name: The Dry Press
rule: After a marked fill, its placement bonuses sleep until an unmarked fill
entrance: A larger framed ink pad appears in the existing header: glossy dark felt marked INKED or pale cracked felt marked DRY, with a drop symbol.
trigger: When readiness changes, the pad compresses to 90 percent then settles over 0.29 seconds; its wet/dry treatment transitions over 0.25 seconds.
persistent: INKED and DRY are printed inside the physical pad. Gloss versus cracks and a crossed dry-drop symbol distinguish states beyond color alone.
notes: This is a stateful pad, not an ink flight from the board. Accessibility explains that an unmarked fill re-inks; the engine controls which immediate bonuses are suppressed.

name: The Review Board
rule: Reach the target and complete a row, a column and a box
entrance: Three paper approval cards show miniature row, column and box diagrams with ROW, COL and BOX labels.
trigger: A newly earned approval compresses then settles over 0.27 seconds. A check badge enters over 0.22 seconds and the approved card receives a sage border and slight tilt.
persistent: Distinct unit diagrams and check badges show which approvals are earned and which remain, while the ordinary target remains in the score HUD.
notes: Approvals reflect committed engine units; neither the card pulse nor a redraw grants approval.

name: The Rival Column
rule: Beat your previous bank or lose 20% of this bank, up to 100 points
entrance: The header invites the player to set a first record, then presents the live bank beside its saved rival benchmark.
trigger: A live comparison meter grows with the bank preview, changing to sage and a checkered flag when the benchmark is beaten. Numerical changes use 0.3-second transitions; the actual bank fee still uses its settlement receipt.
persistent: The header labels the comparison Now to Rival, or Now / Rival beaten. Accessibility includes the exact fee if ending now.
notes: The comparison uses gross bank score; equality does not beat the rival. No new engine benchmark or fee is created by rendering.

name: The Royalty Contract
rule: Each Buff spent adds 5% of the starting target, up to 3 times
entrance: Three unsigned miniature contract slips sit in the header alongside the exact next target increase.
trigger: An actually spent Buff adds a wax signature seal to the next slip with a brief contact-and-settle transition. The real target increases and its existing signature tab shows the change.
persistent: The three slips show exactly how many increases were charged. Next cost comes from the engine; once no increase remains, the contract reads SEALED and Target fixed.
notes: Restoring the same charged seals does not replay their impact. The seals never consume a Buff or apply an increase.

name: The Publicist
rule: Each Bookmark’s flat placement or Line Clear bonus pays once per Turn
entrance: The header shows a paper punchcard counting paid Bookmark bonuses this Turn.
trigger: The shared scoring-source outline identifies an actually paid Bookmark. A larger readable PAID stamp appears on that exact owned copy and the header count updates.
persistent: Each copy retains its PAID stamp for the rest of the Turn. The count and stamps reset next Turn; other effects remain active.
notes: The PAID stamp itself remains static. A count is not a claim that every kind of effect on that Bookmark is disabled.

name: The Word Count
rule: Item bonuses to natural placements share 150 Points per Turn
entrance: A printer symbol, remaining / 150 amount and filled allowance meter occupy the existing header.
trigger: The meter drains with committed extra placement Points and its number transitions over 0.3 seconds. An actual clipped award still shows the existing ruler-like deduction receipt.
persistent: Bonus points left states the remaining shared allowance. The meter resets with the real Turn boundary.
notes: The allowance is for item-added natural-placement Points; base Points and clear bonuses are unchanged. No additional budget is maintained by the view.

name: The Back Page
rule: Natural number values run backwards: 1 scores 90, 9 scores 10
entrance: Each otherwise available Hand card gets a sage price band showing its reversed natural placement value, such as 1 at 90 pts and 9 at 10 pts.
trigger: Price bands use the shared card-object arrival and spring changes. The actual base-Points receipt retains its 0.22-second forward flip when a number scores.
persistent: The printed Point price is visible before committing a card; the digit remains large above it. Header examples remain available.
notes: Prices are natural base Points before other modifiers, not a full award prediction. Bands are absent during frozen scoring; the board and screen do not flip.

name: The Collateral
rule: Target +50%. Before acting, pledge one card for +2 Mult this Turn. Banking returns it.
entrance: An open paper envelope occupies the existing boss header. Selecting an eligible hand tile previews that exact number beside the Pledge action.
trigger: A committed pledge slides the selected tile into the envelope and seals it with a +2 wax seal. A finite anticipation/contact/settle beat accompanies sealing. Banking returns that same tile and reopens preparation for the next Turn.
persistent: The sealed envelope names the pledged number and says it returns at bank. Before a choice, the control distinguishes Pick a tile, Pledge, an ineligible selection, and closed preparation.
notes: +2 Mult is added before ordered Bookmark operations. The pledged tile keeps its identity and is unavailable until bank; no animation mutates inventory or awards Mult.

name: The Split Edition
rule: Fill both editions. Choose where this Turn’s score goes before acting; excess stays in that edition.
entrance: Two small A/B paper stacks appear in the existing header. A brass clip marks the selected destination.
trigger: Selecting a destination moves the brass emphasis. A committed score increase presses a sheet onto the receiving stack with a short lift/contact/settle beat. The engine locks selection after an accepted action until the next Turn.
persistent: Both stacks show their own exact score and target, a progress line, and completion seal. An odd total target is split using each authoritative target rather than rounding them to the same value.
notes: Both editions must meet their target. Direct score awards and banks go to the selected edition; excess never spills into the other. The controls do not add an inventory row.

name: The Last Edition
rule: One bank to win. Start with 4 extra cards and one quarter of the usual target. No extra Turns or rescue.
entrance: A single paper sheet waits between press rails in the existing header. The sheet and ONE BANK label state the limited opportunity.
trigger: Only a real bank event drives the platen anticipation, compression, brief hold, and release. The brass lever lowers and the sheet becomes PRINTED; changing a live score does not trigger the press.
persistent: Before banking, the header shows the live projected score and one available bank. A spent bank shows a neutral printed-sheet mark; victory is decided separately by the engine.
notes: The neutral printed mark does not imply success. No Keep Filling, extra Turns, or rewarded rescue can grant a second bank; animation callbacks never bank score.
